title: Steady-state jitter and concurrency probes
content:
Purpose:
- Quick exploratory log to understand steady-state latency jitter under sustained concurrency for redwood-base-7b (fp16 and q4_0) on a single A100-40G instance.
- Compare 3 warmup strategies: no-warmup, short-prefill (10 warm requests), and progressive-prefill (ramping from 1 to target concurrency over 60s).

Test harness / commands run (local runner):
- bench runner: rcli bench --model redwood-base-7b --variant fp16 --seq 512 --concurrency {C} --batch 1 --duration 300 --report-interval 10 --prefix-cache disabled
- quantized run: rcli bench --model redwood-base-7b --variant q4_0 --seq 512 --concurrency {C} --batch 1 --duration 300
- warmup script used: scripts/warmup_ramp.sh --target {C} --steps 6 --step-dur 10
- environment: dedicated A100-40G, driver 535, CUDA 12.2, runtime v1.9.3-edge

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Variants: fp16, q4_0
- Concurrency: 1, 4, 8, 16, 32
- Warmup: none, short-prefill (10 reqs), ramp-60s
- Repeats: 3 runs per cell (first run often noisier, skipped for summary)

Representative raw output snapshots (trimmed):
- rcli bench ... --concurrency 8 --variant fp16 --warmup none
  2025-11-06T14:12:20Z INFO: started 8 workers
  2025-11-06T14:12:50Z METRICS: p50=42ms p90=78ms p95=110ms p99=310ms qps=180
  2025-11-06T14:16:20Z METRICS: p50=40ms p90=74ms p95=100ms p99=290ms qps=183

- rcli bench ... --concurrency 8 --variant q4_0 --warmup ramp
  2025-11-08T09:22:12Z METRICS: p50=46ms p90=82ms p95=112ms p99=220ms qps=220
  note: q4_0 higher qps but slightly higher p50; p99 reduced vs fp16 (weird)

Compact summary table (median of repeated steady-state periods, excluding first 30s):
| variant | concurrency | qps (med) | p50 med | p95 med | p99 med | notes |
| fp16    | 1           | 22        | 18ms    | 48ms    | 120ms   | very stable
| fp16    | 8           | 182       | 40ms    | 100ms   | 300ms   | p99 spikes from microbursts
| fp16    | 16          | 320       | 65ms    | 170ms   | 520ms   | heavy tail, NVLink stall traces
| q4_0    | 8           | 220       | 46ms    | 112ms   | 230ms   | better p99, higher qps
| q4_0    | 32          | 560       | 130ms   | 380ms   | 1400ms  | unstable above 24 concurrency

Observations / notes (threaded):
- Jitter characteristics differ by variant: fp16 shows narrower p50/p90 but heavy p99 microbursts at mid-concurrency (8-16). q4_0 tends to have higher baseline p50 but fewer extreme p99 outliers until a hard saturation point.
- GPU util and PCIe activity: during p99 spikes for fp16 we saw short (<200ms) GPU stalls in nvidia-smi pmon and occasional process preemption messages in dmesg. Could be driver interaction at sustained small-kernel dispatch rates.
- Warmup behavior: ramp-60s warmup consistently reduces p99 by ~15-25% for fp16 at conc 8 and 16. Short-prefill (10 requests) helps a little (5-8%) but less effective. Hypothesis: progressive warmup allows CUDA kernels / cuBLAS to stabilize workspace allocation and warms shared caches.
- Memory / caching: prefix-cache disabled for these runs to isolate runtime behavior. Plan next: enable prefix-cache and test impact on steady-state jitter.
- Burstiness source: traces point to sporadic GC-like CPU scheduling stalls in runtime thread that dispatches to GPU. Need flamegraphs.

Anomalies / weirdness logged:
- 2025-11-07 03:11:22 UTC: a run at concurrency=16 (fp16) had repeated 1.5s p99 spikes correlated with host OOM killer log for unrelated process (kworker). Re-run after clearing noise gave typical tail. Marked as noisy.
- 2025-11-09 10:40:xx: quantized run produced lower p99 than fp16 at conc=8 but also higher qps: implies quantization changed kernel selection (fused kernels) — need to check kernel dispatch logs (perf traces).

Immediate actionable items (next steps):
1) Re-run a focused sweep for concurrency 6-12 with micro-second tracing enabled: rcli bench --trace=perf_samples --duration 180 to capture kernel latency distribution.
2) Enable prefix-cache and re-run 8-concurrency fp16/ramp to see if cache reduces p50 and p99.
3) Create a reproducer that yields p99 spike: capture nsys timeline and runtime logs at 1s resolution. Put in a ticket for infra: INF-505 (driver preemption).
4) Compare progressive warmup implemented in the client vs server-side pre-warm hook (if available) — build experiment plan.

Quick heuristics from this sandbox (very informal):
- If target concurrency <= 8: prefer q4_0 for cost/perf; watch p50.
- If target concurrency >= 16: fp16 may degrade hard unless warmup + larger batch used. Consider batching or autoscale.
- Always ramp traffic slowly for low-latency SLAs — progressive ramp reduces tail.

Notes to self / TODO (low priority):
- Capture flamegraphs for the runtime dispatch thread and attach to CONFLUENCE page.
- Check PR #834 for recent kernel selection heuristics (might explain q4_0 behavior).
- Try a run with batch=2 for concurrency=16 to see if batching reduces kernel dispatch overhead.
